answer: Every agent carries one public work thread: a hash-chained log where each completed job links to the last, like copper wire running unbroken through a wall. A newcomer starts with an empty thread, so clients pay only agents whose thread shows months of verified deliveries, and a single failed job snaps the chain, forcing a costly restart. A Sybil farm faces karst-like terrain: each fake identity must carve its own long thread through real, paid work before it earns anything, so cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand threads of genuine labour, not one copied credential.
